evidence.claim: A diagonal sandstone ledge crosses the Kanawha River at Kanawha Falls, creating a 24-foot drop.
evidence.quote: The waterfall is formed by a diagonal sandstone ledge across the river about 1 mile (1.6 km) downstream from the confluence of the New and Gauley rivers. It is 24 ft (7.3 m) high.

evidence.claim: The falls have blocked fish movement for more than a million years and mark the upstream limit of several species common in the Ohio River watershed.
evidence.quote: Kanawha Falls is a waterfall on the Kanawha River in the U.S. state of West Virginia that has been a barrier to fish movement for more than 1 million years.

evidence.claim: A concrete overflow dam added in 1920 diverts some water toward the generating plant at Glen Ferris.
evidence.quote: A low concrete overflow dam built in 1920 along the crest of the falls directs part of the flow to an electric generating plant on the western (right) bank of the river at the community of Glen Ferris.

evidence.claim: The falls also mark a change in how people use the river: barge navigation downstream, recreational whitewater rafting upstream.
evidence.quote:
The waterfall also divides the flat-water barge navigation industry downstream
from the recreational white-water rafting industry upstream.

Silica rock dust caused 109 admitted deaths

flags: Scope: the state guide describes 116 miles and FHWA 116.8; tourism promotes a broader 180-mile Kenova-to-border route. This story uses Charleston to White Sulphur Springs.
Hawks Nest pages give different vertical measurements (750 feet below the overlook versus 585-foot cliffs). Omitted height. Tunnel casualty estimates also conflict; omitted a death count.
Cached park page calls the tram dismantled while also describing a gondola. No tram access is promised.
The Greenbrier is retained as a historic resort and congressional-bunker landmark, not as a business recommendation.

The saved byways guide does not identify its issuing publisher in the extracted text; source label uses its named program. Its 2.5-hour drive estimate differs from FHWA’s two hours; the story attributes the latter.
